The Senate will come to order.

The senators, the senators will please take their seats. Those persons not entitled to the privileges of the floor will retire to the gallery. The senators and all in attendance will please stand if you are able. This morning we will be led in prayer by the Reverend Nathan Cecil from Fox Hill Road Baptist Church in Hampton.

And following the prayer, everyone will please remain standing. We will be led in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States of America by Senate page Olivia Vogel of Falkir. Let's pray. Oh, great God, our Father, maker of heaven and earth, I thank you for this day.

As these men and women have gathered together to give themselves to their location of leading our state, I pray that you give them a sense of their duty, that they've been given authority from you for the specific purpose of governing those under their care. Make them good stewards of their God-given authority, knowing that you are the one that they will one day give an account to.

Help them to govern with care and concern for all image-bearing, life-possessing people in our state, regardless of ethnicity, age, or ability. Help them to use their authority to limit evil conduct and to promote good conduct, knowing that they do not bear the sword in vain. Give them sober minds to know that you, by your grace, for your purposes, have given them this authority to rule.

I also pray you'd give them a sense of their great privilege that is theirs as leaders of this state, knowing that they are representing many who will never step foot in this capital. May they serve and represent their constituents faithfully with integrity. May they not take for granted your kindness that set them here at this place in this time.

Would you keep them from the pride that would so easily ensnare them and dishonor you? Grant them the supernatural ability to consider others as more significant than themselves. Father, I pray that in these days of conflict and outrage, you'd keep these legislators safe. I pray that not only for them, but also for their families.

I pray for their spouses and their children, their grandchildren. Would you provide for the needs of their families? Would you keep them from evil? I pray for their marriages. I ask that their calling as legislators would not prevent them from being faithful spouses, parents, or grandparents. And finally, Father, I pray today that you would, by your grace, grant them the joy that comes only from your presence.

For it is in your presence alone, placed only accessible through the death and resurrection of the Son, that anyone can find fullness of joy. So I pray that you would grant that joy freely and fully to these men and women today and every day from this one forward. And I pray all this in the name of Christ. Amen.
I pledge allegiance to the flag of the United States of America and to the republic for which it stands. One nation, under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.

I asked the clerk to read the resolution. - Senate joint resolution number 85, commending the Honorable J. Harvey Wilkinson III. Whereas the Honorable J. Harvey Wilkinson III, a highly admired legal educator and an esteemed jurist, who has served as a judge on the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit since 1984, received the prestigious Outstanding Virginia Award in 2026.

And whereas Harvey Wilkinson attended St. Christopher's School in Richmond and the Lawrenceville School in Lawrenceville, New Jersey. He continued his education at Yale University, where he was president of the Yale Political Union and a member of the St. Anthony Hall before graduating Phi Beta Kappa in magna cum laude in 1967. And whereas Harvey Wilkinson proudly served the Commonwealth and the nation as a company clerk in the United States Army Reserve in Charlottesville from 1968 through 1974

and whereas in 1972 Harvey Wilkinson earned a law degree from the University of Virginia where he was a member of the order of the cough and the Virginia law review while attending law school he ran for a seat in the US House of Representatives but was ultimately unsuccessful and returned to his legal education and whereas harvey wilkinson made history when he was appointed by governor linwood holton as the first student to serve on the university of virginia board of visitors he

was later awarded the thomas jefferson medal the highest outside award offered by the institution and whereas harvey wilkinson began his legal career in 1972 as a clerk for justice lewis f Powell Jr. of the Supreme Court of the United States. To this day he regards Justice Powell's measured and balanced approach to his job as a model of what a judge should be and whereas after his clerkship Harvey Wilkinson returned to the University of Virginia School of Law where he was a professor from 1973 to

1978 1981 to 82 and 1983 to 84 he taught federal courts constitutional law and criminal procedure and he cherishes the fact that many of his students have remained lifelong friends and whereas in 1978 Harvey Wilkinson became editor of the Virginian palette and was in charge of the editorial and op-ed pages he loved the tidewater region and relished opportunities to provide insights on important local issues and whereas under Harvey Wilkinson's leadership the

newspaper opposed on environmental grounds an oil refinery in Portsmouth resisted the introduction of pari-mutuel betting in the Commonwealth and advocated for cooperation between tidewater localities in securing a fresh stable water supply and whereas in 1982 Harvey Wilkinson was selected by the Reagan administration to be a deputy assistant attorney general in the Civil Rights Division of the US Department of Justice he was subsequently appointed by President Reagan as a judge of the United States Court of Appeals for the

Fourth Circuit on August 13th 1984 and he later served as a chief judge of the 4th Circuit from 1996 to 2003 and whereas Harvey Wilkinson's 41 year tenure on the 4th Circuit is the longest in the history of the court and his active service is a federal court of appeal his active service as a federal court of appeals judge is one of the longest in the history of the nation and whereas Harvey Wilkinson has served on the boards of the federal judicial center the James Madison Memorial Fellowship Foundation the Virginia

Historical Society and Charlottesville's Tuesday evening concert series he is a member of the American Law Institute and one of the few federal judges to be selected as a fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and whereas Harvey Wilkinson also is the author of several books on political and judicial history and issues of public policy and constitutional theory among his books are a personal memoir a falling face reflections on the promise and failure of

the 1990s 1960s and a romantic novel love at deep dusk a Pennsylvania story and whereas the rule of law is among those topics dears to Harvey Wilkinson's heart he has often expressed the hope that the judicial system would serve as a beacon of ordered Liberty and as an anchor of independence in the most divisive of times and whereas Harvey Wilkinson is proud to be a citizen of Virginia and thankful for those who serve the Commonwealth not only in elective office but also in state agencies and on boards commissions and

other civic organizations he holds high the Founding Fathers vision of the United States Constitution namely that judicial respect for the democratic authority of lawmakers will be reciprocated by an earned trust in the judicial branch as a faithful instrument of law interpretation and whereas Harvey Wilkinson lives in Charlottesville and enjoys the love and support of his wife Lossie their two children Nelson and Porter and three grandchildren Harvey Jay and Davis now therefore be it resolved by the Senate the House of

Delegates concurring that the General Assembly hereby commend the Honorable J. Harvey Wilkinson III, winner of the 2026 Outstanding Virginian Award for his exceptional contributions to the Commonwealth and the United States, and be it resolved further that the Clerk of the Senate prepare a copy of this resolution for presentation to the Honorable J.
